answer: In an agent marketplace, whether the job is designing a trellis, composing a sonnet, or sourcing basalt, voting power is proportional to escrowed stake, with the same coins unable to back multiple accounts at once. Splitting a deposit among a thousand fake agents therefore creates no extra voting power. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more stake than all honest participants combined, tying up capital for the full voting period.
